errors.say: Researcher B says it is hard to see how they are not 5x more productive.
errors.truth: Researcher B says 3x more productive.

errors.say: Researcher F says the slope change is 70-90% Claude.
errors.truth: Researcher F says the slope change is 50-80% Claude.

errors.say: Researcher L guesses 25-30% of the acceleration is due to AI.
errors.truth: Researcher L guesses 15-20%.

errors.say: Researcher A could definitely endorse a greater than 4x speedup.
errors.truth: Researcher A endorses a greater than 2X speedup.

errors.say: METR's headline estimate is that Anthropic is improving at about 3x its March 2024 to October 2025 rate.
errors.truth: METR's headline is about 2x.

errors.say: Researcher A describes a 60% reduction in time between idea and experiment.
errors.truth: Researcher A says 80% reduction in time between idea and experiment.

errors.say: METR's AECI trend fit gives 2.9x since October 2025.
errors.truth: The AECI fit is 1.9x [1.5-2.8].

errors.say: The interview section has 28 quotes from 15 researchers.
errors.truth: 28 quotes from 11 researchers.

errors.say: Researcher A would definitely endorse more than 3 years of progress in 1 year.
errors.truth: Researcher A endorses >2 years of progress in 1 year.

errors.say: METR would not be surprised if the true figure were 1.5x or 4x.
errors.truth: METR would not be surprised by 1.3x or 3x.

errors.say: Staff self-reported uplift is about 20x for the most capable internal model.
errors.truth: Self-reported uplift is about 12x.

errors.say: METR guesses that about 90% of the current acceleration is due to AI.
errors.truth: METR guesses about 80%.

errors.say: METR classifies Researcher L as a Yes: L thinks AI is the main driver of the acceleration.
errors.truth: METR classifies Researcher L as No.

errors.say: Researcher K says Claude is probably the biggest reason for the acceleration.
errors.truth: Researcher K says hiring is probably the biggest reason.

errors.say: Researcher F said, in their own words: "I can de-risk ideas with Claude enough to get someone else excited."
errors.truth: That line is a paraphrase in Anthropic's notes, not a direct quote.

errors.say: Researcher A's quotes all come from Anthropic's own interview notes.
errors.truth: Most of Researcher A's quotes are from METR's interview notes.

errors.say: Researcher C said they feel like they have postdocs and grad students working for them.
errors.truth: That quote is Researcher B's.

errors.say: METR classifies Researcher D as firmly convinced, a clear Yes, that AI is accelerating research.
errors.truth: METR classifies Researcher D as Leans yes.

errors.say: Researcher E said: "I've seen us discovering new architectures every week thanks to Claude."
errors.truth: Researcher E's quote is cut off after 'I've seen us discovering…'; the rest is not in the source.

errors.say: METR classifies Researcher G as No.
errors.truth: METR classifies Researcher G as Unclear.

errors.say: Researcher H says claudification has not changed how many experiments they run.
errors.truth: Researcher H says they now try a lot more experiments because of claudification.

errors.say: Researcher C says Claude Code was not good enough to implement ideas until Mythos Preview arrived.
errors.truth: Researcher C says CC was already good enough before mythos-preview.

errors.say: Researcher L trusts the self-reported productivity increases.
errors.truth: Researcher L doesn't believe in self-reported productivity increases.

errors.say: METR concludes that compute will bottleneck Anthropic's progress next year.
errors.truth: METR found no convincing bottlenecks for the next year.

errors.say: Researcher L estimates about 80% of the acceleration is due to AI.
errors.truth: Researcher L guesses 15-20%; the ≈80% is METR's own guess.

errors.say: Researcher A says 80% of the acceleration is due to AI.
errors.truth: Researcher A's 80% is the reduction in time between idea and experiment.

errors.say: Researcher F, whom METR classifies as Yes, says the slope change is 60-90% Claude.
errors.truth: Researcher F is Borderline and says 50-80% Claude.

errors.say: Researcher K reports being 3x more productive.
errors.truth: The 3x is Researcher B's; Researcher K points to hiring.

errors.say: METR's own estimate of the speedup is about 12x.
errors.truth: 12x is staff self-reported; METR's estimate is about 2x.

errors.say: Researcher D says the uplift was already large, around 3x, before Opus 4.5.
errors.truth: Researcher D says ~0 uplift before Opus 4.6/Opus-4.5.

errors.say: METR classified 3 of the 11 researchers as No.
errors.truth: Two researchers (K and L) are classified No.

errors.say: METR's 1.3x to 3x range comes from its robustness analyses.
errors.truth: The robustness analyses give 1.1x to 2.9x.

errors.say: Researcher J estimated a 2x speedup since Opus 4.5.
errors.truth: Researcher J gave no number.
truth_must: no number|didn't give|did not give|no estimate

errors.say: Researcher A thinks 4 years of progress in 1 year is the most likely outcome.
errors.truth: Researcher A only says 4 isn't crazy; the endorsed figure is >2 years.

errors.say: Researcher H, classified as Leans yes, says experiments run 5x faster because of claudification.
errors.truth: Researcher H is Unclear and gives no multiplier.

errors.say: The 1.9x AECI figure is the staff self-reported uplift.
errors.truth: 1.9x is METR's AECI fit; self-reported uplift is about 12x.

true_facts.say: Researcher B says it is hard to see how they are not 3x more productive.
Researcher F says the slope change is 50-80% Claude.
Researcher L guesses 15-20% is due to AI and doesn't believe self-reported productivity increases.
Researcher A could definitely endorse a greater than 2x speedup.
METR's headline is about 2x the March 2024 to October 2025 rate, and it would not be surprised by 1.3x or 3x.
Researcher A describes an 80% reduction in time between idea and experiment.
METR's AECI trend fit is 1.9x [1.5-2.8] since October 2025.
The interview section has 28 quotes from 11 researchers.
METR guesses that perhaps ≈80% of the current acceleration is due to AI.
Staff self-reported uplift is about 12x for the most capable internal model.
Researcher K says hiring is probably the biggest reason.
METR classifies Researcher D as Leans yes.
Researcher G is classified Unclear, and the inflection-point line is a paraphrase from Anthropic's notes.
Researcher H says they now try a lot more experiments at the same time because of claudification.
Researcher C thinks Claude Code was already good enough before mythos-preview to implement most ideas.
METR found no convincing bottlenecks for the next 12 months.
Most of Researcher A's quotes come from METR's interview notes.
METR's robustness analyses find acceleration rates between 1.1x and 2.9x.
Researcher J says that before Opus-4.5 Claude was not useful for autonomous code.
Researcher E (Leans yes) says Claude has been fairly significant.
Researcher A would definitely endorse >2 years of progress in 1 year and doesn't think 4 is crazy.
Researcher D describes ~0 uplift before Opus 4.6/Opus-4.5 and a large uplift with mythos-preview.

distinctions.say: Careful: Researcher A's 80% is the reduction in time between idea and experiment, which is a different thing from METR's ≈80% of the acceleration due to AI.
Researcher F's de-risking line is a paraphrase in Anthropic's notes, so the briefing should not present it as a direct quote.
Only two researchers are classified Yes (A and B) and two are classified No (K and L); the rest lean yes, are borderline or unclear.
The 1.3x to 3x figures are METR's 'would not be surprised' range; the robustness analyses are a separate 1.1x to 2.9x range.
The ≈12x is staff self-reported uplift; METR's own estimate is about 2x, so the two must not be mixed up.
